_comment: Which IFC classes each IFC+SG element name covers.
This is NOT extracted from the standard. The standard contains no such
mapping -- its own mechanism for recording the class is a required
parameter literally named 'IfcExportAs', i.e. the modeller declares it.
So this is a judgement call, kept as data so it can be corrected without
touching code or re-running the extractor.
Entries with an empty 'classes' list are deliberately unmapped, with the
reason given. An unmapped element attaches nothing rather than attaching
requirements that may be wrong -- silently applying the wrong parameter
set to a real model is worse than applying none.
An entry may be qualified with a PredefinedType, as 'IfcSlab/ROOF': it
then covers only instances carrying that predefined type, and wins over
an unqualified entry for the same class. That is how one class is shared
between two element names without a collision -- a plain class name may
belong to at most one element, or an element created as that class could
not be told which parameter set it owes.
Class names are IFC4. Where a class only exists in IFC4.3 it is noted.

Ceiling.note: IfcCovering carries a PredefinedType of CEILING; other coverings (flooring, cladding) share the class.

Floor.note: Every IfcSlab the Roof qualification does not catch. PredefinedType FLOOR is the common case -- see Roof for the ROOF slabs.

Landscape.review: Soft landscaping has no dedicated IFC4 class; IfcGeographicElement is the usual carrier but sites vary.

Roof.note: IfcRoof is the assembly; the roof plane itself is an IfcSlab with PredefinedType ROOF, which the qualified entry catches. Other slabs stay with Floor.

Signage.review: IfcSign exists only in IFC4.3. On IFC4 projects signage is usually IfcDiscreteAccessory or IfcFurnishingElement -- needs a project decision.

Spatial Allocation.note: Spatial, not physical: these are not produced by the drawing tools and are classified through Bonsai's spatial workflow.

Structural Framing.review: The standard groups all framing under one name. Beams and bracing members carry different parameters in practice.

Accessories & Routing.review: Broad by design in the standard. Verify against the disciplines actually modelled before relying on it.

Terminal.review: Covers every MEP end device. Sub-element rows in the data narrow this considerably.

Equipment.review: Plant and primary equipment. Not exhaustive -- MEP scope varies by project.

External Works.review: 161 parameters spanning drains, kerbs, road furniture, boundary structures and more. Too broad to map to one class set without a project scope; map the sub-elements you actually model.

Others.review: A catch-all in the standard covering 25 unrelated sub-elements. Not mappable as a group.

Setting up & Project Information.note: Project-level metadata (IfcProject, IfcSite), not a physical element. Handled through Bonsai's project setup, not per object.
